subsystems.name: Target prospecting and selection
subsystems.role: find a carbonaceous (C-type) near-Earth asteroid rich in hydrated minerals and reachable with low velocity change.

subsystems.name: Capture or anchoring
subsystems.role: secure the asteroid or the mining equipment in microgravity so that extraction can proceed.

subsystems.name: Solar heating and extraction
subsystems.role: heat water-bearing regolith until ice and hydrated minerals release water vapour.

subsystems.name: Vapour collection and purification
subsystems.role: condense the water vapour and separate it from other volatiles such as carbon dioxide and ammonia.

subsystems.name: Electrolysis and storage
subsystems.role: split water into hydrogen and oxygen and keep them as cryogenic liquids or high-pressure gas.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: supply electricity for heating, pumping and refrigeration in deep space.

subsystems.name: Propulsion and transfer
subsystems.role: reach the asteroid, then deliver the propellant to a depot or use it in place.

buildSteps.title: Survey and choose a target
buildSteps.detail: Telescope surveys identify C-type asteroids whose spectra show water-bearing clays and whose orbits are easy to reach.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: A robotic spacecraft flies to the asteroid using solar electric propulsion or chemical stages, taking months to years.

buildSteps.title: Rendezvous and characterise
buildSteps.detail: The craft matches the asteroid's orbit, maps its shape and spin, and measures water content with spectrometers or a small lander.

buildSteps.title: Capture or anchor
buildSteps.detail: A small asteroid might be enclosed in a bag; a larger one requires anchoring so a robotic excavator can dig into regolith without pushing itself away.

buildSteps.title: Heat the regolith
buildSteps.detail: Concentrated sunlight, focused by inflatable mirrors, raises the material to roughly 100–200 °C so water sublimates out of the minerals.

buildSteps.title: Collect the water vapour
buildSteps.detail: The vapour is drawn into cold traps, where it freezes onto surfaces chilled by radiators, then melts into liquid water.

buildSteps.title: Electrolyse and store
buildSteps.detail: An electrolyser splits the water into hydrogen and oxygen, which are liquefied by cryocoolers and kept in insulated tanks.

buildSteps.title: Return or depot
buildSteps.detail: The propellant is either used by the mining craft itself or delivered to a storage depot in cislunar space for future missions.

prerequisites.why: JAXA's Hayabusa2 and NASA's OSIRIS-REx returned grams of asteroid material in 2020 and 2023, but no mission has mined or processed volatiles.

prerequisites.tech: In-space cryogenic propellant storage and transfer
prerequisites.why: hydrogen boils away unless actively cooled; long-term storage and transfer of cryogens in space has not been demonstrated at scale.
drilling or digging on a small body tends to push the spacecraft off unless it is firmly anchored, a problem not yet solved in practice.
inflatable solar mirrors have been tested in space, but not for sustained heating of asteroid material.
the International Space Station produces oxygen from water by electrolysis, proving the chemistry works in orbit.
communication delays of minutes to hours mean the mining craft must make many decisions on its own, which is beyond current flight software.

pathway.milestone: sample-return missions have brought back grams of asteroid material for laboratory study
pathway.unlocks: knowledge of which asteroids contain water and how their surfaces behave.

pathway.milestone: a prospecting mission to a C-type near-Earth asteroid measures its water content in situ
pathway.unlocks: selection of a target worth mining.

pathway.milestone: a small-scale extraction demonstration returns a few hundred kilograms of water from an asteroid
pathway.unlocks: proof that the heating, collection and storage steps work in space.

pathway.milestone: commercial extraction and delivery of propellant to a cislunar depot
pathway.unlocks: affordable deep-space transport, because propellant no longer has to be launched from Earth.
